overview.headline: Ballistic throw on the Moon without air drag

keyPoints.point: A thrown ball on the Moon feels no drag and follows purely ballistic flight
keyPoints.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyPoints.point: With no sideways push the horizontal speed stays constant while crossing the ground
keyPoints.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight

keyPoints.point: Vertical speed falls with time while height follows time under steady gravity
keyPoints.quote: The vertical speed is V = V0 - g * t, and the height is y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2.

keyPoints.point: The same throw rises higher on the Moon because gravity there is smaller
keyPoints.quote: Because g on the Moon is about six times smaller, the same throw rises about six times higher than on Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: absence of drag when no air surrounds the thrown ball
